source.title: Memorization in Overparameterized Autoencoders
source.authors: Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan; Karren D. Yang; Mikhail Belkin; C. Uhler

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates memorization and contraction in autoencoders, but does not test natural-label generalization, training-versus-test error gaps, or any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern autoencoder reconstruction and recovery of training examples under iteration. These do not measure the versions' stated behaviors. The paper's introductory statements about generalization cite prior work and are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures autoencoder reconstruction, projection and attraction toward training examples. These are distinct from the classification behaviors, optimizer comparisons, sharpness correlations and example-removal effects specified in V1–V8. Low test reconstruction error alongside attraction does not test V1's natural-versus-random-label comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors characterize projection and attraction toward training examples as autoencoder memorization, show that sufficient convolutional depth enables it, and establish that it can coexist with low reconstruction error. Extension to classification generalization is proposed as a possible mechanism, not demonstrated.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains autoencoders to reconstruct inputs and measures memorization through projection, contraction, recovery, or learned-solution spectra. The claim versions concern classification generalization and train-test error gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Width and depth increase recovery rate in the reported MNIST autoencoder sweep. The paper also reports that initialization affects memorization, with large initialization producing noisy memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected autoencoders project into training-data spans or attract inputs toward individual training examples; tested convolutional autoencoders can also exhibit these behaviors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained overparameterized autoencoders can concentrate their outputs around training examples through projection or attraction.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing width and depth increases training-example recovery probability in the MNIST sweep.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Greater width and depth can strengthen recovery of training examples under autoencoder iteration.

fits_no_version.finding: None of the Table 1 linear convolutional networks memorizes according to the authors' spectral criterion; increasing filters has little effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing filter count does not ensure projection-based memorization in insufficiently deep linear convolutional autoencoders.

fits_no_version.finding: The MNIST model combines train MSE 0.00117 and test MSE 0.00159 with trajectories converging to training examples; an existence theorem also combines attraction with arbitrarily small expected reconstruction error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attraction toward training examples can coexist with low held-out or expected reconstruction error.

record.problems: The empirical contraction and recovery outcomes are mostly qualitative or presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The paper's experiments concern autoencoder reconstruction and memorization rather than classification generalization. The single-layer nonlinear theoretical result relies on stated assumptions and an adaptive-learning-rate variant; the authors note they suspect the adaptive rate may not be necessary but do not establish that empirically.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, natural-label held-out classification accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same training recipe.
Classifier test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Held-out image classification comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks, including local-connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning and alternative training recipes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; this does not negate the reported autoencoder effects. Input-space contraction and the autoencoder Jacobian are distinct from V7's magnitude-scaled weight perturbations.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train classifiers on natural versus random labels or report held-out classification accuracy.
Varies autoencoder width and measures recovery under iteration, not classifier test error across the interpolation threshold.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected classifiers on image-label prediction.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers and SGD on held-out predictive performance.
Does not compare batch sizes or held-out performance under epoch budgets.
Does not test dropout's effect on classifier test error.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with train-test generalization gaps.
Does not remove memorized training examples and measure the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: linear single layer fully connected autoencoder
rows.stage_stated: trained by gradient descent initialized at zero
rows.operation_detail: Fit the autoencoding problem by gradient descent; the solution is characterized as projection onto the training-data span.
rows.value: Maps any input to points in the span of the training set
rows.note: The paper gives this as a known minimum-norm consequence for linear overparameterized regression.
rows.check: An established minimum-norm projection result, also derived in Appendix A; it does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: nonlinear single layer fully connected autoencoder
rows.stage_stated: gradient descent variant initialized at A(0)=0
rows.operation_detail: Train to approximate the training examples under the stated assumptions and adaptive learning rate.
rows.value: φ(A(∞)y) ∈ φ-span(X) for any y ∈ R^d
rows.note: The result is theoretical and conditional on the stated assumptions and gradient-descent variant.
rows.check: Conditional theorem about nonlinear-span membership, not classification generalization.

rows.subject: fully connected autoencoder (10 layers, 512 hidden neurons)
rows.operation_detail: Iterated the trained autoencoder on uniformly spaced initial points from the Swiss Roll dataset.

conditions.value: 100 samples from the 3D Swiss Roll dataset

rows.measure: Convergence of trajectories to training examples
rows.value: Most trajectories converge to training examples
rows.note: The figure caption and accompanying text report the qualitative outcome.
rows.check: Trajectory convergence measures attraction toward training examples, not any listed version.

rows.subject: fully connected autoencoder (7 layers, 128 hidden neurons)
rows.operation_detail: Iterated the autoencoder on random test examples and examined their trajectories.
rows.measure: Convergence of trajectories to training examples
rows.value: Trajectories converge almost exclusively to the training examples
rows.note: The paper does not state a numeric recovery rate for this experiment.
rows.check: Recovery of training images from iterated test inputs does not measure held-out classification performance.

rows.subject: fully connected autoencoder (14 layers, 128 hidden neurons)

rows.note: The paper provides a qualitative result.
rows.check: One-step attraction to training images does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: convolutional autoencoder

rows.subject: nonlinear convolutional autoencoder
rows.stage_stated: trained; number of iterations reported as 1
rows.operation_detail: Tested outputs on arbitrary input images after one iteration.

rows.note: The architecture is described as a downsampling architecture modified with leaky ReLU activations.

rows.subject: fully connected autoencoder (7 layers, 512 hidden neurons)
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction error on the MNIST test set and iterated the model on test examples.

conditions.value: test-image trajectories converge to training examples

rows.note: The caption reports near-zero test reconstruction error and trajectories converging to training examples.
rows.check: The reported train MSE 0.00117 and test MSE 0.00159 are correct, but reconstruction error with attraction does not test V1's random-label fitting and classification comparison.

rows.subject: linear convolutional autoencoders
rows.size_stated: varying layers and filters per layer; exact parameter counts are listed in Table 1
rows.stage_stated: initialized close to zero and trained
rows.operation_detail: Varied layer count and filters per layer while training on random images; assessed memorization from the learned solution spectrum.
rows.measure: Learned-solution spectrum as evidence of memorization
rows.baseline: memorization would be indicated by two eigenvalues that are 1 and remaining eigenvalues close to 0
rows.value: Memorization does not occur in any of the examples; increasing filters per layer has minimal effect on the spectrum
rows.locator: Supplementary Material F, Table 1 and accompanying text
rows.note: The authors explicitly state that none of the listed examples memorizes the two images.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report absent spectral memorization here; that absence concerns autoencoder projection, not any listed version.

rows.subject: linear convolutional autoencoders
rows.size_stated: layers and parameters listed per experiment in Table 2
rows.stage_stated: initialized close to zero and trained; Adam used for depth greater than 10
rows.operation_detail: Trained networks at depths given by a heuristic lower bound and inspected the learned spectrum.

conditions.value: single filter per layer, kernel size 3

rows.measure: Learned-solution spectrum as evidence of memorization
rows.value: Table 2 spectra indicate memorization for the listed experiments
rows.locator: Supplementary Material F, Table 2 and accompanying text
rows.note: The reported experiments vary image size and number of training examples; results are summarized in the table.
rows.check: Spectra concern autoencoder memorization. Several tested depths exceed the tabulated heuristic bound, so the operation should say at or above that bound.

rows.subject: downsampling convolutional autoencoder D1
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the learned solution on standard Gaussian inputs and inspected its spectrum.
rows.value: Spectrum 1, 1, [< 2 · 10−2 ]; outputs a linear combination of training images
rows.locator: Supplementary Material G, Figure 7 and accompanying text
rows.note: The paper states the learned solution has rank exactly 2.
rows.check: The spectrum and output combinations measure linear autoencoder memorization, not a listed version. Describe effective rank rather than treating the reported small residual eigenvalues as proof of exact rank.

rows.subject: downsampling convolutional autoencoder D2
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the learned solution on standard Gaussian inputs and inspected its spectrum.
rows.value: Spectrum 1, [< 7 · 10−6 ]; outputs a multiple of the training image
rows.locator: Supplementary Material G, Figure 8 and accompanying text
rows.note: The paper characterizes the learned solution as rank 1.
rows.check: The spectrum measures linear autoencoder memorization, not a listed version. Small residual eigenvalues support approximate rank one.

rows.subject: fully connected autoencoder
rows.operation_detail: Theorem establishes simultaneous small expected reconstruction error and attraction of training points.
rows.measure: Expected reconstruction error and attractor property

rows.note: This is an existence theorem, not an empirical estimate.
